chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shazan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Barirah had a husband, so when she was emancipated, she was given the choice.'

key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a specific historical figure and slave of Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) used as a primary example in this ruling.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave woman's marriage upon her emancipation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *takhayyur* (choice), granting an emancipated slave woman the right to decide whether to remain in her existing marriage or separate, as her status changes from property to a legal person. This ruling, attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlights the juristic distinction between the continuity of marriage for free persons and the conditional nature of marriage for slaves, ensuring her autonomy upon manumission. It serves as a foundational text in Shia fiqh for understanding the intersection of slavery, marriage contracts, and individual agency.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Bureyra had a husband for her. So when she was emancipated, she had a choice (to be with him or not)’.
